title: Bogong moths can migrate using an internal geomagnetic compass
description:
Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03693-w

Australian migratory moths navigate long distances, in part owing to a stellar ‘compass’. It transpires that they have another compass that detects the inclination, or angle, of Earth’s magnetic field lines and that probably relies on a light-dependent quantum-mechanical mechanism similar to the one found in night-migratory songbirds.
